title: Dakar Rally 2026
tagline: The world's toughest cross-country rally raid returns to Saudi Arabia for a seventh consecutive edition.
shortDescription: The 48th Dakar Rally ran across Saudi Arabia from 3-17 January 2026, starting and finishing in Yanbu on the Red Sea coast. It drew 812 competitors from 69 countries in 433 vehicles.
description:
The Dakar Rally is the most demanding off-road endurance event in motorsport, and the 2026 edition marked the seventh consecutive year that Saudi Arabia hosted the full route. Organised by France's Amaury Sport Organisation (A.S.O.) and supported by the Saudi Ministry of Sport and the Saudi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation, the rally ran from 3 to 17 January 2026 with Yanbu on the Red Sea coast serving as both start and finish.

The 2026 route threaded through AlUla, Hail, Riyadh, Wadi Al-Dawasir, Bisha and Al-Hanakiyah, mixing high-speed gravel tracks with the deep dune fields of the Empty Quarter. Competition categories covered cars, motorcycles, quads, lightweight prototypes, trucks and the Dakar Classic regularity class, plus the Mission 1000 division for low-emission and alternative-energy prototypes that the organisers use as a technology testbed.

For Saudi Arabia the Dakar is a flagship of the Quality of Life Program under Vision 2030 and a significant driver of regional tourism and hospitality demand, with 812 competitors of 69 nationalities and thousands of team personnel, media and spectators moving across the Kingdom for two weeks. The rally also functions as a shop window for Saudi motorsport infrastructure ahead of the country's wider motorsport ambitions.
whatToExpect: Bivouac villages that relocate almost daily, open to accredited teams and media, with live service parks and briefing tents. Public spectator zones are set up at ceremonial start and podium locations in Yanbu and at selected stage areas. Expect early-morning starts, live stage tracking, and heavy media presence from international broadcasters.
venueName: Yanbu start/finish with stages across the Saudi desert
venueAddress: Yanbu, Al Madinah Province, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Amaury Sport Organisation (A.S.O.) with the Saudi Ministry of Sport

title: Future Minerals Forum 2026
tagline: Riyadh's global mining summit convening ministers, miners and investors around the super-region from Africa to Central Asia.
shortDescription: The fifth Future Minerals Forum ran 13-15 January 2026 at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Center in Riyadh under the theme 'Dawn of a Global Cause', with a ministerial roundtable and an investor-focused exhibition.
description:
The Future Minerals Forum (FMF) is Saudi Arabia's flagship mining and critical-minerals platform, launched in 2022 by the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources as part of the Kingdom's push to make mining the third pillar of its industrial economy alongside oil and petrochemicals. The fifth edition ran from 13 to 15 January 2026 at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Center in Riyadh under the theme 'Dawn of a Global Cause'.

FMF is built around the 'super-region' concept, a mineral-rich corridor running from Africa through the Middle East to Central and South Asia. The programme pairs a ministerial roundtable, one of the largest gatherings of mining ministers anywhere, with technical conference tracks on exploration, downstream processing, ESG and responsible sourcing, mine financing, and workforce development. The forum is also the venue at which Saudi Arabia typically announces exploration licence rounds and updates to its estimated mineral wealth.

Attendees include mining company executives, sovereign and institutional investors, geological survey agencies, equipment and technology vendors, and multilateral bodies such as the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative. For MENA business audiences, FMF matters because it links Saudi industrial policy, energy-transition supply chains and cross-border investment into one calendar moment, and because deals and MoUs signed at the event frequently shape the following year's project pipeline.
whatToExpect: A conference floor at KAICC with plenary and parallel technical stages, a ministerial programme running in parallel, and an exhibition of mining technology, geological survey services and national pavilions. Expect heavy delegation traffic, structured investor matchmaking, and side events run by geological surveys and multilateral organisations.
venueAddress: King Abdulaziz Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources, Saudi Arabia

title: Big 5 Construct Saudi Winter Edition 2026
tagline: The winter staging of Saudi Arabia's largest construction trade event at Riyadh Front.
shortDescription: Big 5 Construct Saudi's winter edition ran 18-21 January 2026 at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, co-located with specialist shows for facades, landscaping and stone.
description:
Big 5 Construct Saudi is the Kingdom's largest construction industry trade event, organised by dmg events, which also runs The Big 5 in Dubai. Because of the sheer volume of Saudi construction activity tied to Vision 2030 giga-projects, the show has run multiple editions per year; the winter edition took place from 18 to 21 January 2026 at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center.

The exhibition covers the full building supply chain: building materials and concrete, MEP and HVAC, construction tools and heavy equipment, smart building technology, and finishing and interiors. It is co-located with focused shows including the Windows, Doors & Facades Event, Urban Design & Landscape Expo and Marble & Stone, which lets contractors and developers source across categories in a single visit.

Visitors are dominated by Saudi contractors, developers, consultants, government project owners and procurement teams, with international exhibitors arriving in country pavilions from China, Turkey, Italy, India and the Gulf. Alongside the exhibition, dmg runs free-to-attend CPD-certified workshops and leadership summits covering construction technology, modular methods, sustainability compliance and project delivery in the Saudi regulatory environment.
whatToExpect: Multiple exhibition halls organised by product sector, with live product demonstrations and heavy machinery on display. Free CPD-certified talks run on in-hall stages throughout the four days. Expect large contractor delegations, on-stand negotiation, and country pavilions clustered by region.
venueAddress: Riyadh Front, Airport Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Historic Jeddah Winter Season 2026
tagline: Heritage-led winter programming across Al-Balad, the UNESCO-listed historic district of Jeddah.
shortDescription: A winter cultural and tourism season staged in Historic Jeddah (Al-Balad) in early 2026, combining restored heritage houses, craft markets, performances and guided heritage trails.
description:
Historic Jeddah, known locally as Al-Balad, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the historic core of the Red Sea port city, famous for its coral-stone merchant houses and carved wooden rawasheen balconies. The Historic Jeddah Winter Season is a seasonal programme run under the Ministry of Culture's Historic Jeddah Program that opens restored buildings and public squares to visitors during the cooler months.

The season combines heritage interpretation with contemporary cultural programming: guided walking trails through the restored districts, craft and artisan markets, traditional Hijazi food, live music and theatre in the historic squares, and exhibitions installed inside restored merchant houses. It sits alongside the wider restoration effort that has seen dozens of historic buildings stabilised and reopened as museums, galleries, cafés and boutique guesthouses.

The season matters commercially because Al-Balad has become the anchor of Jeddah's cultural tourism proposition and the host district for the Red Sea International Film Festival. For the hospitality, F&B and creative sectors it is a proving ground for adaptive reuse of heritage assets, and for the Ministry of Culture it demonstrates how heritage districts can be made economically productive without losing their fabric.
whatToExpect: Evening-weighted programming through narrow historic lanes and courtyards, with pop-up markets, craft workshops, food stalls and live performance stages. Expect guided heritage tours, restored houses open to the public, and heavy footfall on weekends.
venueAddress: Al-Balad, Historic Jeddah, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Ministry of Culture — Historic Jeddah Program

title: AlUla Arts Festival 2026
tagline: A month of contemporary art, performance and design across AlUla's oasis and AlJadidah Arts District.
shortDescription: The fifth AlUla Arts Festival ran 16 January to 14 February 2026, turning the AlUla oasis and AlJadidah Arts District into an open-air gallery of contemporary art, performance and design.
description:
The AlUla Arts Festival is the visual-arts anchor of the AlUla Moments cultural calendar, staged by the Royal Commission for AlUla in the ancient oasis valley of north-west Saudi Arabia. The fifth edition ran from 16 January to 14 February 2026, concentrated in the AlJadidah Arts District and spilling into the oasis, Old Town and the surrounding desert landscape.

Programming spans commissioned installations, gallery exhibitions, artist residencies through the Madrasat Addeera and AlUla Arts Residency programmes, design showcases, film screenings and live performance. The festival runs concurrently with Desert X AlUla, the site-specific land-art exhibition, which means visitors in this window can see both an urban-scale arts district programme and large-scale desert commissions in a single trip.

For the Saudi creative economy the festival is significant as a year-round employment and skills pipeline rather than a one-off event: it feeds the AlUla creative industries strategy, supports local artisans in weaving, ceramics and jewellery, and brings international curators, collectors and press into a region that the Kingdom is positioning as a global cultural destination alongside its archaeology.
whatToExpect: Walkable arts district with galleries, studios and commissioned installations, plus outdoor performance spaces and evening programming under desert skies. Expect artist talks, workshops open to the public, and shuttle links to Desert X AlUla installations in the wider valley.
venueName: AlJadidah Arts District and AlUla Oasis
venueAddress: AlJadidah, AlUla, Medina Province, Saudi Arabia

title: Desert X AlUla 2026
tagline: Site-specific land art staged across the AlUla desert, themed 'Space Without Measure'.
shortDescription: The fourth edition of Desert X AlUla ran 16 January to 28 February 2026, presenting ten new site-specific commissions in the AlUla desert inspired by the poetry of Kahlil Gibran.
description:
Desert X AlUla is a recurring land-art exhibition created as a collaboration between the Royal Commission for AlUla and Desert X, the organisation behind the Coachella Valley biennial in California. It places large-scale, site-specific commissions directly into the sandstone canyons and open desert of AlUla, free to visit and navigable by a marked driving and walking route.

The fourth edition ran from 16 January to 28 February 2026 under the theme 'Space Without Measure', presenting ten new works by a multigenerational group of Saudi, regional and international artists responding to the poetry of Kahlil Gibran. The commissions engage with the geology, light and scale of the valley, and several are designed to change appearance through the day as shadows move across the rock faces.

Desert X AlUla is a central plank of AlUla's strategy to build an internationally credible contemporary-art programme alongside its archaeological assets at Hegra and Dadan. It draws curators, critics and collectors into the region, generates significant international press coverage, and supports a growing local ecosystem of fabricators, guides and hospitality operators serving cultural tourism.
whatToExpect: A free, self-guided open-air exhibition trail through the desert with parking areas and marked approaches to each artwork. Guides and shuttle options are available from AlUla town. Expect early-morning and late-afternoon visits for the best light, plus talks and guided curator walks on selected dates.
venueAddress: AlUla, Medina Province, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Royal Commission for AlUla with Desert X

title: Saudi Franchise Expo 2026
tagline: The Kingdom's dedicated franchising marketplace, connecting international brands with Saudi master franchisees.
shortDescription: Saudi Franchise Expo 2026 ran 26-28 January 2026 at The Arena Riyadh, gathering franchise brands, master franchisees and investors around the Kingdom's fast-growing franchising sector.
description:
The Saudi Franchise Expo is the Kingdom's dedicated trade platform for the franchising sector, organised by Sunaidi Expo and Conferences and held from 26 to 28 January 2026 at The Arena Riyadh venue for exhibitions. It brings together franchisors looking for Saudi market entry, existing Saudi franchise groups seeking new concepts, and the legal, financing and fit-out service providers that surround franchise deals.

Franchising has become an explicit policy priority in Saudi Arabia. The Franchise Law and the accompanying franchise disclosure regime introduced by the Ministry of Commerce gave the sector a formal regulatory footing, and Monsha'at's SME support programmes actively promote franchising as a route for Saudi entrepreneurs to acquire proven operating models. The expo sits at the intersection of those policies and the private capital chasing food and beverage, retail, fitness, education and services concepts.

The 2026 edition featured around 139 exhibitors under the patronage of the Ministry of Commerce leadership, with a programme aligned to Vision 2030 goals for non-oil sector development and entrepreneurship. Visitors are largely Saudi investors and family offices evaluating concepts, alongside regional franchise consultants and international brands running structured market-entry meetings.
whatToExpect: A compact exhibition floor of franchise brand stands with dedicated meeting areas for investor conversations, plus a seminar programme on franchise law, unit economics and market entry. Expect one-to-one matchmaking between franchisors and prospective Saudi franchisees.
venueName: The Arena Riyadh — Venue for Exhibitions
venueAddress: The Arena, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: IFAT Saudi Arabia 2026
tagline: Environmental technologies for water, sewage, waste and recycling brought to Riyadh by Messe München.
shortDescription: IFAT Saudi Arabia 2026 ran 26-28 January 2026 at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, covering water and wastewater treatment, waste management and recycling technology.
description:
IFAT is the world's leading trade fair brand for environmental technologies, run by Messe München, and IFAT Saudi Arabia is its Kingdom edition. The 2026 event took place from 26 to 28 January at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, covering water and wastewater treatment, sewerage networks, solid waste management, recycling and the circular economy, and municipal service technology.

The Saudi context makes this a strategically important show. The Kingdom is one of the world's largest desalinated-water producers, is investing heavily in wastewater reuse targets under the National Water Strategy, and has established the National Center for Waste Management to drive landfill diversion and recycling rates upward from a low base. Those mandates create a substantial procurement pipeline for pumps, membranes, sensors, sorting equipment and treatment plant EPC services.

Exhibitors range from German, Italian and Chinese equipment manufacturers to Saudi water utilities, environmental service operators and engineering consultancies. Visitors are dominated by municipal and regional authority engineers, industrial plant operators managing effluent, and contractors bidding on giga-project utility packages. The accompanying conference programme addresses regulation, reuse standards and the economics of circular infrastructure in the Gulf.
whatToExpect: An exhibition hall of treatment equipment, pumps, sorting machinery and monitoring technology, with live demonstrations on larger stands. A conference programme runs alongside covering water reuse, waste policy and circular-economy business models. Expect strong municipal and utility delegation attendance.
venueAddress: Riyadh Front, Airport Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Real Estate Future Forum 2026
tagline: Riyadh's senior real-estate policy and investment forum, themed 'Expanding Horizons: Real Estate Thriving'.
shortDescription: The fifth Real Estate Future Forum ran 26-28 January 2026 at the Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh, Kingdom Centre, convening more than 10,000 delegates around Saudi and global real-estate investment.
description:
The Real Estate Future Forum (REFF) is Saudi Arabia's senior-level real-estate conference, distinct from trade exhibitions in that it is built around policy, capital allocation and market structure rather than exhibitor sales. The fifth edition ran from 26 to 28 January 2026 at the Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh in Kingdom Centre under the theme 'Expanding Horizons: Real Estate Thriving', welcoming more than 10,000 delegates.

The agenda typically covers housing supply and affordability under the Sakani programme, REIT and real-estate debt markets, the giga-project development pipeline including Diriyah, Qiddiya, NEOM and New Murabba, PropTech and digital transaction infrastructure, hospitality and branded residences, and cross-border capital flows into and out of the Kingdom. Sessions bring together ministers and regulators, developer CEOs, sovereign wealth and pension allocators, and international investment managers.

For MENA business audiences REFF is one of the clearest read-outs on where Saudi real-estate capital is heading in a given year, and it has become the venue at which major development partnerships and regulatory signals — such as changes to foreign ownership rules or new financing instruments — are discussed publicly by the people setting them.
whatToExpect: A hotel-based conference format with plenary keynotes, moderated panels and parallel tracks, plus a compact exhibition of developers and platforms. Networking is concentrated in structured meeting lounges and evening receptions. Expect a heavily senior delegate list and simultaneous Arabic/English interpretation.
venueName: Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh, Kingdom Centre
venueAddress: Kingdom Centre, King Fahd Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Space Debris Conference 2026
tagline: The Saudi Space Agency's international forum on orbital debris and long-term space sustainability.
shortDescription: The second International Space Debris Conference took place 26-27 January 2026 in Riyadh, organised by the Saudi Space Agency with participation from 75 countries.
description:
The Space Debris Conference is organised by the Saudi Space Agency (SSA) as a dedicated international forum on orbital debris mitigation, space traffic coordination and the long-term sustainability of the orbital environment. The second edition ran on 26 and 27 January 2026 in Riyadh, drawing participation from 75 countries under the framing of a global platform for the future of space.

The technical agenda addresses debris measurement and cataloguing, conjunction assessment and collision avoidance, active debris removal and end-of-life disposal, on-orbit servicing, and the regulatory and liability questions raised by rapidly growing satellite constellations. Delegates come from national space agencies, defence and civil space-situational-awareness operators, satellite manufacturers and operators, insurers, academic research groups and international bodies working on space governance.

The conference is part of Saudi Arabia's broader effort to establish itself as a credible participant in space governance rather than only a customer of space services. The Kingdom has established its own space agency and regulatory framework, has flown Saudi astronauts to the International Space Station, and is investing in downstream Earth-observation and satellite-communications capability. Hosting a debris and sustainability conference positions Riyadh inside the multilateral conversation on orbital rules of the road.
whatToExpect: A conference-format event with technical paper sessions, policy panels and international agency briefings, held in a hotel conference centre. Expect a strongly institutional delegate mix of agencies, operators and academics, with structured bilateral meetings between national space authorities.
venueAddress: Al Faisaliah Center, Olaya, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Riyadh Marathon 2026
tagline: The Kingdom's flagship mass-participation road race, hosted by the Saudi Sports for All Federation.
shortDescription: The fifth Riyadh Marathon ran 28-31 January 2026, based at Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University, with full marathon, half marathon and shorter community distances.
description:
The Riyadh Marathon is Saudi Arabia's flagship mass-participation running event, organised by the Saudi Sports for All Federation as part of the Quality of Life Program under Vision 2030. The fifth edition ran from 28 to 31 January 2026, based at Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University in Riyadh, with the race weekend structured around a full marathon plus half marathon and shorter community distances.

The event has grown quickly from a domestic community race into an internationally recognised fixture, attracting elite and club runners from across the Gulf, Africa and Europe alongside tens of thousands of recreational participants. It carries an expo component where running brands, nutrition companies, health insurers and fitness operators reach a large consumer audience during race-number collection.

Beyond sport, the marathon functions as a public-health and city-activation instrument. Saudi Arabia has used mass-participation events to raise physical-activity rates, particularly among women, and the Riyadh Marathon's route through the city doubles as a showcase for urban development. For sponsors it is one of the largest single-day consumer touchpoints on the Saudi calendar outside the entertainment seasons.
whatToExpect: A multi-day format with a runner expo and race-pack collection ahead of race day, then staggered starts by distance from the university campus. Expect large crowds, on-course entertainment, and a finish-area festival with sponsor activations and recovery zones.
venueAddress: Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2026
tagline: Saudi Arabia's contemporary art biennale at the JAX District, titled 'In Interludes and Transitions'.
shortDescription: The third Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale ran 30 January to 23 April 2026 at the JAX District in Diriyah, curated under the title 'In Interludes and Transitions'.
description:
The Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale is Saudi Arabia's principal contemporary-art biennale, staged by the Diriyah Biennale Foundation in the JAX District, a converted industrial warehouse quarter on the edge of Diriyah that has become Riyadh's main contemporary-art and creative-industries campus. The third edition ran from 30 January to 23 April 2026 under the title 'In Interludes and Transitions', led by artistic directors Nora Razian and Sabih Ahmed.

The biennale presents commissioned and existing works by Saudi, regional and international artists across large warehouse galleries and outdoor spaces, accompanied by a public programme of talks, performances, film screenings, workshops and a research strand. Its curatorial framing typically engages with questions of time, transition and cultural change, which in the Saudi context reads directly against the pace of national transformation.

The Diriyah Biennale Foundation also organises the Islamic Arts Biennale in Jeddah, alternating the two so the Kingdom hosts a major international art event most years. For the art market and the Saudi creative economy, the biennale is significant infrastructure: it professionalises curatorial and technical production capacity locally, builds an audience for contemporary art, and gives Saudi artists a platform with international critical attention.
whatToExpect: Large converted warehouse galleries with room-scale installations, plus outdoor commissions in the JAX District. Free or low-cost entry with guided tours, a bookshop, cafés and a rolling public programme of talks and performances across the three-month run.
venueAddress: JAX District, Diriyah, Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia

title: Saudi Media Forum 2026
tagline: The Kingdom's flagship media industry gathering, held with the FOMEX media technology exhibition.
shortDescription: The Saudi Media Forum ran 2-4 February 2026 in Riyadh under royal patronage, convening around 300 media leaders alongside the FOMEX media and technology exhibition.
description:
The Saudi Media Forum (SMF) is the Kingdom's principal annual gathering for the media and communications industry, held under the patronage of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques and organised in partnership with the Saudi Ministry of Media and the Saudi Broadcasting Authority. The 2026 edition ran from 2 to 4 February at the Hilton Riyadh, convening around 300 media leaders from across the Arab world and internationally.

The programme addresses the structural pressures reshaping Arab media: the economics of digital-first newsrooms, the impact of generative AI on production and verification, streaming and content localisation, media measurement and advertising markets, misinformation, and regulation. Sessions mix broadcasters, publishers, platform executives, regulators, agencies and academics, and the forum has become the main venue where regional media strategy is debated in public.

SMF runs alongside FOMEX, the Future Media Expo, a trade exhibition of broadcast and production technology, studio equipment, streaming infrastructure and media-tech vendors. That pairing gives the event both an editorial-strategy dimension and a procurement dimension, and it supports Saudi Arabia's stated ambition to build a regional content-production hub tied to its wider entertainment and film investments.
whatToExpect: A hotel conference programme of keynotes and panels running alongside the FOMEX exhibition floor of broadcast and media technology. Expect large Arab-media delegations, awards and recognition segments, and workshops for working journalists and producers.
venueAddress: Eastern Ring Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Saudi Media Forum with the Ministry of Media

title: RLC Global Forum Annual Meeting 2026
tagline: Global retail leadership convening in Riyadh under the 2026 theme 'Growth Crossroads'.
shortDescription: The RLC Global Forum Annual Meeting was held 3-4 February 2026 in Riyadh under the theme 'Growth Crossroads', bringing retail CEOs, brand owners and investors together.
description:
The RLC Global Forum, which grew out of the Retail Leaders Circle MENA Summit, is a senior invitation-led retail conference that has made Riyadh its annual meeting venue. The 2026 edition ran on 3 and 4 February under the theme 'Growth Crossroads', reflecting a period in which Gulf retail is absorbing rapid e-commerce growth, new mall and mixed-use supply, and shifting consumer behaviour.

The agenda covers retail real estate and the future of physical space, omnichannel and quick-commerce economics, franchise and brand licensing structures, luxury and premium retail in the Gulf, supply chain and localisation requirements, and the entry of international brands into Saudi Arabia. Delegates are predominantly C-suite: retail group CEOs, mall operators, brand principals, private equity and family-office investors, and the consultancies serving them.

Saudi Arabia matters to this audience because it is the largest consumer market in the GCC by population, with a young demographic, rising female labour-force participation and a rapid build-out of retail and leisure destinations tied to giga-projects. RLC is where much of the deal conversation about brand entry, master franchise rights and joint-venture structures happens in a concentrated two days.
whatToExpect: A closed-door style conference with keynote sessions, CEO panels and curated networking rather than a large exhibition floor. Expect structured one-to-one meeting programmes between brands and potential Saudi partners, plus evening networking receptions.
venueAddress: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Saudi Interiors & Furniture Expo Jeddah 2026
tagline: Jeddah's trade exhibition for interior design, furniture and fit-out at the Jeddah Superdome.
shortDescription: An international trade exhibition for interior design, furniture and fit-out held at the Jeddah Superdome in early February 2026, serving the western region's residential and hospitality projects.
description:
The Saudi Interiors and Furniture Expo is the western region's trade platform for interior design, furniture manufacturing and fit-out, staged at the Jeddah Superdome. It gives suppliers direct access to the Makkah Province market, which combines a large domestic residential base with heavy hospitality investment tied to Hajj and Umrah capacity expansion and Red Sea tourism development.

Exhibitors span furniture manufacturers and importers, textiles and soft furnishings, lighting, flooring and surfaces, kitchen and bathroom systems, and fit-out contractors. Visitors include interior designers and architects, hotel and hospitality procurement teams, developers, retailers and distributors, and a significant share of end consumers on public days, which distinguishes it from strictly B2B shows.

The sector context is strong: Saudi Arabia's housing programmes have pushed large volumes of new residential units into the market, hotel keys under development in Jeddah and along the Red Sea run into the tens of thousands, and localisation policy is encouraging domestic furniture manufacturing rather than pure import. The show also functions as a design-trend showcase, with feature areas presenting contemporary Saudi and regional interior styling.
whatToExpect: A single-venue exhibition floor of furniture and interiors stands with staged room sets and material displays, plus designer talks and trend features. Expect a mix of trade buyers during business hours and consumer visitors in the evenings.
venueAddress: Madinah Road, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia

title: Saudi International Dental Conference 2026
tagline: The 37th SIDC, the Saudi Dental Society's flagship scientific congress and dental trade exhibition.
shortDescription: The 37th Saudi International Dental Conference ran 5-7 February 2026 at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, with around 7,350 participants and more than 130 exhibiting companies.
description:
The Saudi International Dental Conference (SIDC) is organised by the Saudi Dental Society and is the largest dental scientific meeting in the Kingdom. The 37th edition ran from 5 to 7 February 2026 at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, combining an accredited scientific programme with a substantial commercial exhibition.

The scientific programme features more than 100 international speakers across lectures, hands-on workshops and specialist sessions covering restorative and aesthetic dentistry, implantology, endodontics, orthodontics, oral surgery, paediatric dentistry, digital workflows and intraoral scanning, and practice management. Continuing-education credit makes attendance professionally valuable for Saudi and regional practitioners.

The accompanying exhibition hosted more than 130 local and international companies presenting dental units and chairs, imaging and CAD/CAM systems, materials and consumables, and clinic software. Expected attendance was around 7,350 participants with 47 exhibitors registered at announcement. SIDC alternates and complements a Jeddah edition, giving the Saudi Dental Society national reach across both the central and western regions.
whatToExpect: Parallel lecture halls and hands-on workshop rooms running alongside a dental trade exhibition. Expect live clinical demonstrations on equipment stands, poster sessions from Saudi dental schools, and CE-accredited session tracking for practitioners.
venueAddress: Riyadh Front, Airport Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: World Defense Show 2026
tagline: Saudi Arabia's biennial all-domain defence exhibition, staged at its purpose-built venue north of Riyadh.
shortDescription: The third World Defense Show ran 8-12 February 2026 in Riyadh, an all-domain defence exhibition organised under the General Authority for Military Industries covering air, land, sea, security and space.
description:
The World Defense Show (WDS) is Saudi Arabia's biennial international defence exhibition, established in 2022 and owned by the General Authority for Military Industries (GAMI). The third edition ran from 8 to 12 February 2026 at the purpose-built World Defense Show exhibition complex north of Riyadh near King Khalid International Airport, with its own runway and live-demonstration areas.

WDS is positioned as an all-domain show, covering air, land, sea, security and space rather than specialising in one service branch. Exhibitors include the major global primes, national pavilions from allied and partner states, and a growing tier of Saudi manufacturers and joint ventures built around Saudi Arabian Military Industries (SAMI) and GAMI's localisation mandate. The show features flying displays, live ground demonstrations and static aircraft and vehicle parks.

The strategic driver is Saudi Arabia's target to localise 50 percent of military spending domestically by 2030, one of the most consequential industrial-policy goals in the region. WDS is therefore as much a procurement and offset-negotiation venue as an exhibition: partnership agreements, technology-transfer arrangements and joint-venture announcements cluster around the event, and it draws senior military and government delegations from across the Middle East, Africa, Asia and Europe.
whatToExpect: A vast purpose-built site with indoor exhibition halls, outdoor static displays of aircraft, armoured vehicles and naval systems, and scheduled flying and live-fire style demonstrations. Access is trade and delegation-focused, with structured VIP delegation routes and a conference programme running alongside.
venueAddress: North of King Khalid International Airport, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: PIF Private Sector Forum 2026
tagline: The Public Investment Fund's forum opening its portfolio companies' supply chains to Saudi private business.
shortDescription: The fourth PIF Private Sector Forum ran 9-10 February 2026 at KAICC in Riyadh, expecting over 12,000 private-sector participants, 200-plus speakers and 100-plus sessions across six stages.
description:
The PIF Private Sector Forum is the Public Investment Fund's annual mechanism for connecting Saudi and international private companies to the procurement pipelines of its portfolio companies and giga-projects. The fourth edition ran on 9 and 10 February 2026 at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Center in Riyadh, with more than 12,000 private-sector participants expected, over 200 speakers and more than 100 sessions across six stages.

The forum exists because PIF is now among the largest sovereign investors in the world and its portfolio — spanning NEOM, Qiddiya, Diriyah, Roshn, Red Sea Global, Cruise Saudi, Saudi Arabian Military Industries, Lucid and dozens of others — represents an enormous concentrated demand signal. The event gives SMEs and larger suppliers a structured route into that demand through procurement briefings, supplier registration clinics, and one-to-one meetings with portfolio-company sourcing teams.

Programming covers sector deep-dives, localisation requirements and in-Kingdom value-add rules, financing and working-capital solutions for suppliers, and capability-building for Saudi SMEs. For MENA business audiences it is one of the most practical events on the calendar: attendance translates directly into supplier qualification opportunities rather than only thought leadership.
whatToExpect: A high-volume forum with six parallel stages, portfolio-company pavilions staffed by procurement teams, supplier registration desks and pre-booked matchmaking meetings. Expect long queues at major portfolio-company stands and a strongly transactional atmosphere.
venueAddress: King Abdulaziz Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Jeddah E-Prix 2026
tagline: Formula E's night-race double-header on the Jeddah Corniche Circuit.
shortDescription: The 2026 Jeddah E-Prix ran on 13 and 14 February 2026 as a double-header on the Jeddah Corniche Circuit, forming rounds four and five of the 2025-26 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.
description:
The Jeddah E-Prix is Saudi Arabia's round of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship, held on the Jeddah Corniche Circuit alongside the Red Sea. The 2026 running took place on 13 and 14 February as a double-header, providing rounds four and five of the 2025-26 season, raced under floodlights in the evening.

Formula E has raced in Saudi Arabia since 2018, initially at Diriyah, where the series staged the first night races in its history against the backdrop of the UNESCO-listed At-Turaif district. The move to the Jeddah Corniche Circuit puts the all-electric championship on the same street layout used by Formula 1, one of the fastest street circuits in world motorsport, and links the event to Jeddah's waterfront regeneration.

The race weekend is bundled with entertainment programming including concerts and fan activations, and it carries a clear policy message: Saudi Arabia uses Formula E to signal its investment in electric mobility, renewable generation and the localisation of EV manufacturing through PIF's stakes in Lucid and the Ceer national EV brand. Teams, manufacturers and technology suppliers use the paddock for commercial and government engagement across the region.
whatToExpect: A compact street-circuit race weekend with practice, qualifying duels and two evening races, plus grandstand and hospitality access along the Corniche. Expect fan zones, driver appearances, concerts after racing, and an open-paddock culture that is unusually accessible for top-tier motorsport.
venueAddress: Jeddah Corniche, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: ABB FIA Formula E World Championship

title: Saudi Cup 2026
tagline: The world's richest horse race, run over two days at King Abdulaziz Racecourse in Riyadh.
shortDescription: The seventh Saudi Cup was held 13-14 February 2026 at King Abdulaziz Racecourse in Riyadh, with the $20 million feature race on the Saturday and total prize money of $39.6 million.
description:
The Saudi Cup is the world's richest horse race and the centrepiece of the Riyadh racing season, run by the Jockey Club of Saudi Arabia at King Abdulaziz Racecourse. The seventh edition took place across 13 and 14 February 2026, with the $20 million feature race on the Saturday and a two-day card carrying total prize money of $39.6 million.

The meeting has become a fixture of the international thoroughbred calendar, drawing runners from the United States, Japan, Europe and the Gulf. Alongside the main dirt-track feature, the card includes turf group races, an international jockeys challenge, and purebred Arabian racing that connects the meeting to Saudi Arabia's own equestrian heritage. International horses typically begin arriving around ten days before the meeting for quarantine and acclimatisation.

Beyond sport, the Saudi Cup is a substantial soft-power and tourism event, with hospitality villages, fashion programming and concerts around the racing. It anchors a broader Saudi investment in equestrian sport that includes ownership stakes in international bloodstock and the development of racing infrastructure, and it draws a concentrated international media and high-net-worth audience into Riyadh in February.
whatToExpect: A two-day race meeting with grandstand and hospitality tiers, a paddock and parade ring open to spectators, and international broadcast operations on site. Expect fashion and hospitality programming, live music after racing, and heavy attendance by international owners, trainers and bloodstock agents.
venueAddress: King Abdulaziz Racecourse, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Makkah Halal Forum 2026
tagline: The third edition of the halal industry forum staged in the holy city of Makkah.
shortDescription: Makkah Halal Forum 2026 ran 14-16 February 2026 at the Makkah Chamber Exhibitions and Events Center under the theme 'Halal: A Professional Industry'.
description:
The Makkah Halal Forum is an international platform for the halal economy hosted in the holy city of Makkah and supported by the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development alongside the Makkah Chamber. The third edition ran from 14 to 16 February 2026 at the Makkah Chamber Exhibitions and Events Center under the theme 'Halal: A Professional Industry'.

The forum treats halal as an industrial and standards question rather than only a religious certification matter. Programming covers halal certification and accreditation harmonisation across jurisdictions, traceability and supply-chain assurance technology, halal pharmaceuticals and cosmetics, Islamic finance instruments supporting halal trade, and export access to the OIC market. It combines a conference with a business exhibition and structured B2B meetings.

Saudi Arabia has strategic reasons to lead here: the Kingdom established the Saudi Halal Center under the Saudi Food and Drug Authority to build domestic certification capability, and the halal economy is a targeted non-oil export sector. Holding the forum in Makkah also connects it directly to the pilgrim-services economy, where food, cosmetics and pharmaceutical supply chains serve millions of visitors annually.
whatToExpect: A conference programme in Arabic and English with parallel technical sessions on certification and standards, alongside an exhibition of halal producers, certification bodies and logistics providers. Expect structured B2B matchmaking and delegations from OIC member states.
venueName: Makkah Chamber Exhibitions and Events Center
venueAddress: Makkah Chamber, Makkah, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development with Makkah Chamber

title: Riyadh International Book Fair 2026
tagline: The Kingdom's largest publishing event and one of the biggest book fairs in the Arab world.
shortDescription: The Riyadh International Book Fair ran 13-23 March 2026, organised by the Literature, Publishing and Translation Commission, with hundreds of publishers and a large cultural programme.
description:
The Riyadh International Book Fair is the Kingdom's largest publishing event and one of the biggest book fairs in the Arab world, organised by the Literature, Publishing and Translation Commission of the Ministry of Culture. The 2026 edition ran from 13 to 23 March, drawing publishers, distributors, literary agents and hundreds of thousands of readers over eleven days.

The fair combines a commercial trade element — rights trading, distribution deals and publisher stands from across the Arab world, Europe and Asia — with an extensive public cultural programme of author talks, poetry readings, panel discussions, translation workshops, children's programming and theatrical performances. A guest-of-honour country programme brings a national publishing delegation and cultural presentation each year.

The fair is central to Saudi Arabia's cultural-sector strategy. The Literature, Publishing and Translation Commission uses it to grow the domestic publishing industry, support translation into and out of Arabic, and professionalise the rights market. For regional publishers it is one of the most commercially significant fairs on the Arabic-language calendar, given the size of the Saudi reading market and public library and institutional purchasing.
whatToExpect: Very large exhibition halls filled with publisher stands selling directly to the public, plus dedicated seminar theatres running a dense daily cultural programme. Expect long evening opening hours, family attendance, book signings and a separate professional rights area.
venueAddress: 2446 King Abdullah Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Literature, Publishing and Translation Commission, Ministry of Culture

title: Taif Rose Festival 2026
tagline: Six weeks of rose harvest, distillation and heritage programming in the highland city of Taif.
shortDescription: The Taif Rose Festival runs through the spring harvest season, typically from March into April, celebrating the Damask rose farms and traditional distillation industry of Taif.
description:
The Taif Rose Festival celebrates the annual Damask rose harvest in the highland city of Taif, where hundreds of farms and dozens of traditional distilleries produce rose water and rose oil that is used, among other things, in the washing of the Kaaba. The festival typically opens in March as the harvest begins and runs for around six weeks into April, timed to the flowering season rather than to fixed calendar dates.

Programming centres on the farms and factories themselves: visitors can watch the dawn picking, tour distilleries where petals are steam-processed in copper stills, and buy rose products directly from producers. Around this sits a heritage and family programme of markets, folk performances, poetry, craft workshops and food, staged in the city and at the King Fahd Garden festival grounds.

Economically the festival supports a distinctive agricultural cluster that Saudi Arabia has been formalising through geographic-origin protection and quality standards for Taif rose products. It is also a pillar of the Kingdom's domestic tourism strategy for the Makkah Province highlands, drawing visitors from Jeddah, Makkah and Riyadh into a cooler mountain destination and extending Taif's season beyond the summer.
whatToExpect: Farm and distillery visits during the early-morning harvest, plus a festival site with producer stalls, rose-product retail, craft demonstrations and evening cultural performances. Expect strong domestic-family attendance and heavy weekend traffic on the Taif mountain roads.
venueName: Taif rose farms and festival grounds
venueAddress: Taif, Makkah Province, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Taif Municipality with the Ministry of Tourism

title: Saudi Travel Market 2026
tagline: The Kingdom's B2B travel and tourism trade exhibition at RICEC in Riyadh.
shortDescription: Saudi Travel Market 2026 ran 29-31 March 2026 at the Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center, connecting destinations, operators, hotels and travel technology suppliers.
description:
The Saudi Travel Market (STM) is the Kingdom's dedicated business-to-business travel and tourism exhibition, held from 29 to 31 March 2026 at the Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center. It brings together national tourism boards, destination management companies, hotel groups, airlines, tour operators, travel agencies and travel technology providers targeting the Saudi outbound and inbound markets.

Saudi Arabia is simultaneously one of the largest outbound travel markets in the Middle East and one of the fastest-growing inbound destinations, following the introduction of tourist visas and heavy investment in destinations including AlUla, the Red Sea, Diriyah and Qiddiya. STM sits at that intersection: international destinations compete for Saudi travellers while Saudi destinations, operators and Ministry of Tourism bodies court international trade partners.

The exhibition is paired with a conference programme covering religious tourism and the Hajj and Umrah supply chain, luxury and adventure travel product development, distribution and OTA dynamics, aviation capacity, and tourism investment. Buyers include Saudi travel agency networks, corporate travel managers and religious-tourism operators, which makes the show commercially direct rather than purely promotional.
whatToExpect: National and destination pavilions alongside hotel, airline and technology stands, with a hosted-buyer programme running pre-scheduled meetings. Expect a conference stage on the show floor, product-launch presentations and destination cultural activations.
venueAddress: 2446 King Abdullah Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Future Aviation Forum 2026
tagline: GACA's global aviation forum in Riyadh, themed 'Unlocking Global Growth, Designing the Future Sky'.
shortDescription: The Future Aviation Forum ran 20-22 April 2026 at KAICC in Riyadh, hosted by GACA and expected to welcome more than 12,000 aviation leaders from over 150 countries.
description:
The Future Aviation Forum (FAF) is hosted by the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) of Saudi Arabia and has become one of the largest civil-aviation policy gatherings outside the ICAO assembly cycle. The 2026 edition ran from 20 to 22 April at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Center in Riyadh under the theme 'Unlocking Global Growth, Designing the Future Sky', with more than 12,000 aviation leaders expected from over 150 countries.

The agenda covers air connectivity and route development, airport capacity and infrastructure investment, sustainable aviation fuel and decarbonisation, air-traffic management modernisation, advanced air mobility, and the regulatory frameworks needed for all of it. Participants include civil aviation regulators, airline and airport chief executives, aircraft and engine manufacturers, air navigation service providers, lessors and infrastructure investors.

Saudi Arabia's own aviation strategy gives the forum weight: the Kingdom is targeting 330 million passengers and 150 destinations by 2030, has launched Riyadh Air as a second national carrier, and is building King Salman International Airport in Riyadh as one of the world's largest airport projects. FAF is where those plans are presented to the global industry and where aircraft orders, route agreements and infrastructure partnerships are frequently announced.
whatToExpect: A large conference with ministerial plenaries, CEO panels and technical breakouts, supported by an exhibition of airlines, airports, manufacturers and technology suppliers. Expect major commercial announcements, bilateral government meetings and a heavy international delegation presence.
venueAddress: King Abdulaziz Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Capital Markets Forum Riyadh 2026
tagline: Saudi Tadawul Group's flagship capital-markets gathering connecting global investors to the Saudi Exchange.
shortDescription: The Capital Markets Forum was held 28-30 April 2026 in Riyadh, organised by Saudi Tadawul Group as the anchor event of its global CMF programme.
description:
The Capital Markets Forum (CMF), formerly branded the Saudi Capital Market Forum, is organised by Saudi Tadawul Group and is the principal annual meeting point between the Saudi Exchange and international institutional capital. The Riyadh edition ran from 28 to 30 April 2026, positioned as the anchor event of a broader CMF programme that Tadawul has extended with satellite editions in Hong Kong and New York.

The forum's agenda covers equity and debt market development, index inclusion and foreign-investor flows, IPO pipeline and listing reform, derivatives and market infrastructure, sukuk and Islamic finance, asset management growth, and the regulatory agenda set by the Capital Market Authority. Speakers are drawn from exchange leadership, global asset managers, investment banks, sovereign investors, listed-company CFOs and market regulators.

The Saudi Exchange is the largest stock market in the Middle East by market capitalisation and has been one of the most active IPO venues globally in recent years, so the forum carries genuine allocation significance for emerging-market investors. It is also where Tadawul Group communicates market-structure changes — settlement, market-making, single-stock derivatives and foreign ownership mechanics — to the international investor base.
whatToExpect: A conference-format event with keynote sessions, issuer and investor panels and closed-door institutional roundtables, plus structured corporate-access meetings between listed Saudi companies and international fund managers. Expect a senior finance-sector delegate list.
venueAddress: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Human Capability Initiative 2026
tagline: Saudi Arabia's global human capital conference, themed 'The Human Code' with the UK as country of honour.
shortDescription: The Human Capability Initiative Conference 2026 convened in Riyadh in early May 2026 under the theme 'The Human Code', expecting more than 15,000 participants and 250-plus speakers.
description:
The Human Capability Initiative (HCI) is Saudi Arabia's flagship conference on human capital development, delivered under the Human Capability Development Program, one of the Vision 2030 realisation programmes. The 2026 conference was staged in Riyadh in early May under the theme 'The Human Code', with the United Kingdom named country of honour and more than 15,000 global participants expected.

The programme spans education systems reform, lifelong learning and reskilling, the labour-market implications of artificial intelligence and automation, health and wellbeing as components of human capability, culture and values, and the measurement frameworks used to benchmark national human capital. Speakers include education and labour ministers, university leaders, employers, EdTech founders, multilateral organisations such as the OECD and UNESCO, and researchers.

HCI matters commercially because Saudi Arabia is one of the largest buyers of education, training and workforce technology in the region, and the conference functions as a marketplace for those services alongside its policy role. It also acts as a bilateral diplomacy venue, with the country-of-honour mechanism used to deepen education and skills partnerships — in 2026 with the UK's universities, awarding bodies and training providers.
whatToExpect: A large conference with plenary keynotes, thematic tracks and interactive workshop formats, supported by an exhibition of universities, training providers and education technology companies. Expect ministerial-level delegations, international university pavilions and structured partnership signings.
venueAddress: King Abdulaziz Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Automechanika Riyadh 2026
tagline: Messe Frankfurt's automotive aftermarket and service trade fair for the Saudi market.
shortDescription: Automechanika Riyadh 2026 ran 4-6 May 2026 at the Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center, covering parts, accessories, workshop equipment and vehicle service technology.
description:
Automechanika Riyadh is the Saudi edition of Messe Frankfurt's global Automechanika brand, the world's largest trade fair network for the automotive service industry. The 2026 edition ran from 4 to 6 May at the Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center, covering parts and components, tyres and batteries, accessories and customising, workshop tools and diagnostic equipment, car wash and care, and electric-vehicle service technology.

The Saudi aftermarket is one of the largest in the Middle East, driven by a big vehicle parc, long average ownership and high annual mileage. At the same time the market is changing quickly: electric vehicles are being introduced through Lucid's Saudi manufacturing, the Ceer national EV brand and PIF-backed charging infrastructure, which creates new demand for EV-capable workshop equipment and technician training.

Exhibitors are dominated by parts manufacturers and distributors from China, Turkey, India, Korea, Germany and the Gulf, organised into country pavilions. Visitors are workshop owners, fleet operators, parts distributors and retailers, and dealer service managers. A technical programme runs alongside covering diagnostics, EV servicing, workshop management and counterfeit-parts enforcement.
whatToExpect: An exhibition floor grouped by product category with country pavilions, live workshop-equipment demonstrations and technician training sessions. Expect strong distributor and workshop-owner attendance and on-stand price negotiation.
venueAddress: 2446 King Abdullah Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Saudi Entertainment and Amusement Expo 2026
tagline: SEA Expo, the Kingdom's trade show for theme parks, attractions and location-based entertainment.
shortDescription: SEA Expo 2026 ran 4-6 May 2026 at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, serving Saudi Arabia's fast-expanding attractions, theme park and entertainment venue sector.
description:
The Saudi Entertainment and Amusement Expo (SEA Expo) is the Kingdom's dedicated trade show for the attractions and location-based entertainment industry, organised by dmg events and held from 4 to 6 May 2026 at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center. It covers theme park rides and equipment, family entertainment centres, water parks, arcade and redemption games, immersive and VR attractions, cinema technology, and venue operations and safety systems.

The show exists because Saudi Arabia has become one of the world's most active entertainment-infrastructure markets. The General Entertainment Authority licenses thousands of events annually, Qiddiya is building a full-scale entertainment city outside Riyadh including Six Flags Qiddiya City and the Aquarabia water park, and mall operators and PIF-backed developers are commissioning family entertainment centres at scale across the Kingdom.

Exhibitors include international ride manufacturers, game and simulator suppliers, ticketing and access-control platforms, and turnkey FEC developers. Visitors are venue operators, mall and destination developers, government entertainment bodies, and investors evaluating the sector. A conference programme runs alongside covering attraction design, operations, safety standards and the economics of Saudi entertainment assets.
whatToExpect: A show floor with working rides, simulators, arcade machines and VR attractions that visitors can try, alongside supplier stands and a conference stage. Expect operator and developer delegations, and hands-on product testing rather than static displays.
venueAddress: Riyadh Front, Airport Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Beautyworld Saudi Arabia 2026
tagline: Messe Frankfurt's beauty, hair, fragrance and wellbeing trade fair for the Saudi market.
shortDescription: Beautyworld Saudi Arabia 2026 ran 18-20 May 2026 at the Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center, covering cosmetics, hair, fragrance, personal care and salon equipment.
description:
Beautyworld Saudi Arabia is the Kingdom's edition of Messe Frankfurt's Beautyworld trade fair network, held from 18 to 20 May 2026 at the Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center. It covers cosmetics and skincare, hair products and salon equipment, fragrance and oud, nail and personal care, packaging and private label, and wellness and spa.

Saudi Arabia is the largest beauty and personal care market in the GCC by value, with distinctive category strengths in fragrance — particularly oud and Arabian perfumery — and rapid growth in colour cosmetics and skincare driven by a young population and expanding e-commerce and social commerce channels. Localisation policy is also encouraging domestic manufacturing and private-label production rather than pure import distribution.

Exhibitors range from international brand principals and contract manufacturers to Saudi and Gulf perfume houses, distributors and packaging suppliers. Visitors are retailers and pharmacy chains, salon and spa owners, distributors and importers, e-commerce operators and beauty entrepreneurs. The show programme typically includes salon competitions, live styling and make-up demonstrations, and sessions on regulation, halal certification for cosmetics, and retail trends.
whatToExpect: An exhibition floor organised into fragrance, cosmetics, hair and packaging zones, with live styling stages, product sampling and country pavilions. Expect distributor negotiations, private-label sourcing meetings, and a strong presence of Saudi perfume houses.
venueAddress: 2446 King Abdullah Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Sharqiah Season 2026
tagline: The Eastern Province's entertainment and culture season across Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran.
shortDescription: Sharqiah Season is the Eastern Province edition of Saudi Arabia's entertainment seasons, running across Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran in the late spring and early summer of 2026.
description:
Sharqiah Season is the Eastern Province instalment of Saudi Arabia's calendar of regional entertainment seasons, run under the General Entertainment Authority. It spreads programming across the Dammam metropolitan area, Khobar's corniche, Dhahran and coastal and island locations in the province, typically during the late spring and early summer window.

The season combines concerts by Arab and international artists, sports events, theatre and comedy, family carnivals and zones, food festivals, and marine and beach activities that take advantage of the Gulf coastline. It also draws heavily on the province's distinctive character as the historic centre of the Saudi oil industry and home to a large expatriate and Aramco-linked community, as well as its proximity to Bahrain via the King Fahd Causeway.

Economically the seasons programme is designed to redistribute domestic tourism and entertainment spending away from Riyadh and Jeddah into the regions, supporting local hospitality, retail and event-services businesses. For brands and event suppliers, Sharqiah Season is the main annual opportunity to reach the Eastern Province consumer market at scale, and it creates significant short-term demand for staging, security, catering and temporary infrastructure.
whatToExpect: Multiple activation zones across Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran with ticketed concerts, family carnival areas, food and retail markets, and waterfront events. Expect evening-weighted programming, ticketing through national platforms, and heavy weekend attendance.
venueName: Venues across Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran
venueAddress: Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia

title: Jeddah Season 2026
tagline: Jeddah's summer entertainment season on the Red Sea, part of the wider Saudi Summer programme.
shortDescription: Jeddah Season 2026 opened on 20 June as part of the Saudi Summer programme, with entertainment, concerts, sport and waterfront activations across the Red Sea city.
description:
Jeddah Season is the Red Sea city's entry in Saudi Arabia's calendar of entertainment seasons, run by the General Entertainment Authority and in 2026 opening on 20 June as part of the wider Saudi Summer programme that spans Jeddah, Asir, the Red Sea coast, Taif and Al Baha.

The season programmes concerts by regional and international artists, sporting events, theatre and comedy, family zones and carnivals, marine and beach activities along the Corniche, and food and retail markets. It leans on Jeddah's assets — the waterfront, the historic Al-Balad district, King Abdullah Sports City and a dense hospitality base — and typically runs through the summer holiday period when domestic travel peaks.

The commercial logic is straightforward: summer is historically when Saudi families travelled abroad, and the seasons programme is designed to retain that spending domestically while building the events and hospitality industry. For Jeddah specifically the season supports hotel occupancy, F&B and retail through the hottest months, and it feeds a growing local supply chain of production, staging, talent booking and event-management firms.
whatToExpect: Multiple activation zones across the city and Corniche with ticketed concerts, family entertainment areas, beach and marine activities, and pop-up dining and retail. Expect late-evening programming to avoid summer heat and ticketing through national platforms.
venueName: Venues across Jeddah including the Corniche and Al-Balad
venueAddress: Jeddah, Makkah Province, Saudi Arabia

title: Saudi Plastics and Petrochem 2026
tagline: Riyadh's international trade exhibition for plastics processing, petrochemicals and polymer technology.
shortDescription: Saudi Plastics & Petrochem 2026 ran 21-24 June 2026 at the Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center, covering polymer processing machinery, raw materials and recycling technology.
description:
Saudi Plastics & Petrochem is the Kingdom's long-running trade exhibition for the plastics and petrochemical processing industries, held from 21 to 24 June 2026 at the Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center. It covers injection moulding, extrusion and blow moulding machinery, polymer raw materials and additives, moulds and tooling, recycling and compounding equipment, and automation for plastics plants.

The show's relevance rests on Saudi Arabia's position as one of the world's largest polymer producers through SABIC, Aramco's downstream operations and the industrial clusters at Jubail and Yanbu. Government policy is pushing hard to move value downstream from resin export into domestic conversion and finished-goods manufacturing, which creates continuing demand for processing machinery and technical know-how among Saudi converters.

The exhibition runs alongside Saudi Print & Pack, giving packaging converters and printers a combined sourcing platform, and it draws exhibitor pavilions from China, Taiwan, Turkey, India, Germany and Italy. Visitors are plastics processors, packaging manufacturers, industrial buyers, plant engineers and distributors serving the Gulf market, with an increasing focus on recycled content and circular-economy compliance.
whatToExpect: Large halls of working processing machinery with live demonstrations, material supplier stands and tooling displays. Expect technical seminars, machinery commissioning discussions and a strongly engineering-led visitor profile.
venueAddress: 2446 King Abdullah Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Saudi Print and Pack 2026
tagline: The 21st international trade exhibition for printing and packaging technologies in Riyadh.
shortDescription: Saudi Print & Pack 2026 ran 21-24 June 2026 at RICEC in Riyadh, co-located with Saudi Plastics & Petrochem and covering printing presses, converting and packaging machinery.
description:
Saudi Print & Pack is the Kingdom's dedicated exhibition for printing and packaging technology, holding its 21st edition from 21 to 24 June 2026 at the Riyadh International Convention & Exhibition Center. It is co-located with Saudi Plastics & Petrochem, which places resin producers, converters, printers and packaging buyers under one roof.

The product scope covers offset, flexographic and digital printing presses, labelling and coding systems, corrugated and folding-carton converting, flexible packaging, finishing and binding, packaging design and prepress software, and end-of-line automation. Sustainability is a growing theme, with recyclable and mono-material packaging, reduced-plastic formats and food-contact compliance featuring in both exhibits and seminars.

Demand drivers in Saudi Arabia include a large domestic food and beverage manufacturing base, growing pharmaceutical and cosmetics production, e-commerce packaging volumes, and localisation rules that favour in-Kingdom converting over imported finished packaging. Visitors are commercial printers, packaging converters, brand-owner packaging engineers, and distributors of consumables and spare parts across the Gulf.
whatToExpect: Working presses and converting lines demonstrated live on the show floor alongside consumables and software stands. Expect technical seminars on packaging sustainability and print automation, and a mix of Saudi converters and regional distributors negotiating equipment deals.
venueAddress: 2446 King Abdullah Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Future Hospitality Summit Saudi Arabia 2026
tagline: The Kingdom's hospitality investment and deal-making forum, themed 'Where opportunity meets capital'.
shortDescription: FHS Saudi Arabia 2026 ran 22-24 June 2026 at Mandarin Oriental Al Faisaliah in Riyadh, with more than 150 speakers and investors representing trillions in assets under management.
description:
The Future Hospitality Summit (FHS) Saudi Arabia is the Kingdom's leading hospitality investment conference, organised by The Bench and held from 22 to 24 June 2026 at Mandarin Oriental Al Faisaliah in Riyadh under the theme 'Where opportunity meets capital'. The 2026 edition featured more than 150 speakers and drew investors collectively representing several trillion dollars in assets under management.

FHS is a deal-making forum rather than a trade show. The agenda covers hotel development pipelines and brand signings, asset management and operator selection, financing structures for hospitality real estate, tourism demand forecasting, branded residences, and the operating fundamentals of new Saudi destinations including the Red Sea, AlUla, Diriyah, Qiddiya and NEOM.

The scale of the Saudi hospitality pipeline is what draws international capital: the Kingdom has tens of thousands of hotel keys under development, a tourism strategy targeting 150 million annual visits by 2030, and sovereign-backed developers actively seeking operating partners. FHS is the concentrated moment where owners, operators, lenders and advisers meet, and management agreements and brand entries are frequently announced around it.
whatToExpect: A hotel-based conference with keynote interviews, investor panels and closed roundtables, supported by dense pre-arranged one-to-one meetings between owners and operators. Expect senior attendance, evening networking receptions and deal announcements timed to the event.
venueAddress: Al Faisaliah Center, Olaya, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Saudi Film Festival 2026
tagline: The 12th Saudi Film Festival at Ithra in Dhahran, themed 'Every Story is a Journey'.
shortDescription: The 12th Saudi Film Festival ran in late June and early July 2026 at the King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra) in Dhahran, after being rescheduled from its original April dates.
description:
The Saudi Film Festival is the Kingdom's longest-running film festival, hosted at the King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra) in Dhahran in the Eastern Province and organised with the Saudi Cinema Association. The 12th edition ran in late June and early July 2026 under the theme 'Every Story is a Journey', having been rescheduled from its original April dates because of regional instability.

Unlike the glamour-focused Red Sea festival in Jeddah, the Saudi Film Festival is a filmmaker's festival with an industry and craft emphasis. It runs competitive sections for Saudi and Gulf feature films, documentaries, short films and screenplays, alongside a production market, masterclasses, a film book publishing strand and critical seminars. Its awards, the Golden Palm trophies, are among the most meaningful recognitions for Saudi filmmakers.

The festival matters to the Saudi screen sector because it predates the reopening of cinemas in 2018 and provided continuity for a filmmaking community that had no theatrical outlet. Today it functions as a talent pipeline for the Film Commission, Ithra's production initiatives and the wider commercial industry, and its documentary strand in particular has become an important venue for Saudi work exploring identity, heritage and social change.
whatToExpect: Screenings in Ithra's cinema and theatre spaces with post-screening Q&As, plus masterclasses, a production market and industry panels. Expect a filmmaker-heavy audience, book launches and exhibitions on Saudi cinema history in Ithra's galleries.
venueName: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra)
venueAddress: Ithra, Dhahran, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia

title: WWE Night of Champions 2026
tagline: WWE's premium live event returning to Riyadh's Kingdom Arena.
shortDescription: WWE Night of Champions was staged at Kingdom Arena in Riyadh on Saturday 27 June 2026, part of WWE's long-term partnership with Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority.
description:
WWE Night of Champions is one of the company's premium live events and was staged at Kingdom Arena in Riyadh on Saturday 27 June 2026. It forms part of the long-running partnership between WWE and Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority, under which the Kingdom hosts multiple major WWE events each year with championship matches booked specifically for the Saudi cards.

Kingdom Arena, located in the Boulevard City district of Riyadh, is a large indoor venue built to host arena-scale entertainment and combat sports, and it has become the default home for international wrestling, boxing and MMA events in the capital. The WWE events are broadcast globally, giving them a soft-power dimension well beyond ticket revenue.

The partnership sits inside a broader Saudi sports-entertainment strategy that also includes major boxing promotions through Riyadh Season, UFC events, and the WWE announcement that WrestleMania will be staged in Saudi Arabia in 2027, the first time the event has been held outside the United States or Canada. For the domestic events industry these shows are significant training grounds for large-scale production, security and broadcast operations.
whatToExpect: A single-night arena show with full WWE production, entrance staging and pyrotechnics, broadcast live worldwide. Expect fan meet-and-greet activations around Boulevard City, merchandise stands and a family-heavy live audience.
venueAddress: Boulevard City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: WWE with the General Entertainment Authority

title: Saudi Water Week 2026
tagline: The inaugural Saudi Water Week in Jeddah, hosting the Arab Water Forum and World Water Forum consultations.
shortDescription: The first Saudi Water Week ran 28 June to 2 July 2026 in Jeddah, hosting the Arab Water Forum and consultation meetings ahead of the 11th World Water Forum in Riyadh in 2027.
description:
Saudi Water Week is a new flagship platform launched by the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, with its inaugural edition running from 28 June to 2 July 2026 in Jeddah. It consolidates several water events into a single week, including the Arab Water Forum and the second stakeholder consultation meeting for the 11th World Water Forum, which Saudi Arabia will host in Riyadh in 2027.

The programme comprised more than 97 dialogue sessions plus specialised workshops and technical presentations covering desalination technology and energy intensity, treated-wastewater reuse, water governance and regulation, agricultural water efficiency, non-revenue water reduction, and water security for arid regions. Participants included Arab water ministers, utilities, desalination technology companies, development banks and research institutions.

Saudi Arabia's stake in this is direct and large. The Kingdom is among the world's biggest producers of desalinated water, has committed to major increases in treated-wastewater reuse, and has restructured its sector around the Saudi Water Authority and the Saudi Water Partnership Company procurement model. Hosting the World Water Forum in 2027 makes Saudi Water Week the primary preparatory venue, and it concluded by setting a roadmap for that event.
whatToExpect: A week-long series of ministerial sessions, technical forums and workshops with an accompanying exhibition of water technology and utilities. Expect Arab-region ministerial participation, multilateral development bank presence and a strong technical desalination and reuse focus.
venueAddress: Jeddah, Makkah Province, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

title: Esports World Cup 2026
tagline: Seven weeks of elite competition in Riyadh with a prize pool of around $75 million across 24 titles.
shortDescription: The Esports World Cup 2026 ran in Riyadh from 6 July to 23 August 2026, crowning champions across more than 20 game titles with a prize pool of roughly $75 million and a Club Championship.
description:
The Esports World Cup is the largest competitive gaming event in the world by prize money, staged annually in Riyadh by the Esports World Cup Foundation. The 2026 edition ran across seven weeks from 6 July to 23 August, with a prize pool of around $75 million distributed across more than twenty game titles plus the overarching Club Championship that rewards organisations for consistent performance across the whole programme.

The format is deliberately cross-title: rather than a single-game tournament, EWC runs sequential competitions in fighting games, MOBAs, shooters, battle royales, sports simulations, strategy and mobile titles, with a points system aggregating club performance. The Club Support Program pays participating organisations to field rosters across multiple titles, which has materially changed the economics of professional esports teams globally.

The event is the centrepiece of Saudi Arabia's National Gaming and Esports Strategy, which targets gaming as a growth sector for the non-oil economy and is backed by the Savvy Games Group and PIF's stakes in publishers and platforms. Beyond the competition itself, EWC hosts a large public festival, developer showcases and an industry conference programme, and it draws hundreds of thousands of visitors to Riyadh during the summer.
whatToExpect: Purpose-built competition arenas in Riyadh's Boulevard City with public festival zones, publisher activations, cosplay and creator meet-ups. Expect ticketed finals, extensive global broadcast, and a rolling schedule where different titles occupy the venue in successive weeks.
venueAddress: Boulevard City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Big 5 Construct Saudi 2026
tagline: Saudi Arabia's largest construction event, co-located with the Saudi Industrial Expo at Riyadh Front.
shortDescription: Big 5 Construct Saudi returns 30 August to 2 September 2026 at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, covering the full construction supply chain with free CPD-certified workshops.
description:
Big 5 Construct Saudi is the Kingdom's largest construction industry event, organised by dmg events. The main 2026 edition runs from 30 August to 2 September at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, co-located with the Saudi Industrial Expo, Saudi Wood Expo and the Saudi Warehousing & Logistics Expo, creating a combined built-environment and industrial sourcing platform.

The exhibition covers building materials and concrete, MEP, HVAC and plumbing, construction tools and heavy machinery, smart building and construction technology, and finishing, interiors and surfaces. Country pavilions bring large delegations of manufacturers from China, Turkey, Italy, India, Germany and the Gulf, while Saudi manufacturers use it to demonstrate compliance with local-content requirements.

The demand backdrop is exceptional: Saudi Arabia has one of the world's largest active construction pipelines, spanning giga-projects, the Sakani housing programme, transport infrastructure including the Riyadh Metro and rail expansion, and the stadium and venue build-out for the 2034 FIFA World Cup and Expo 2030.
