That reflects the way Saudi developers now use Cityscape as a primary sales channel for off-plan launches, and it makes the event one of the largest single real-estate sales moments anywhere in the world.
whatToExpect: Enormous exhibition halls with developer sales stands, scale models and immersive project experiences, alongside conference stages on urban development and investment. Expect very heavy public footfall, on-site sales and mortgage desks, and major project launches timed to the show.
venueAddress: Malham, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Informa Markets with the Saudi Ministry of Municipalities and Housing

title: Seamless Saudi Arabia 2026
tagline: Payments, fintech, e-commerce and retail technology converging at Riyadh Front.
shortDescription: Seamless Saudi Arabia runs 17-18 November 2026 at Riyadh Front, bringing more than 4,500 attendees and 200 exhibitors across payments, fintech, e-commerce, retail and digital marketing.
description:
Seamless Saudi Arabia is Terrapinn's Kingdom edition of the Seamless brand, held on 17 and 18 November 2026 at Riyadh Front. It covers the convergence of payments, fintech, digital banking, e-commerce, retail, home delivery and digital marketing, with more than 4,500 attendees and around 200 exhibitors expected.

The show's distinctive angle is that it treats commerce end to end rather than isolating fintech. Content tracks run across payment acceptance and processing, embedded finance and buy-now-pay-later, digital banking platforms, marketplace and D2C e-commerce operations, logistics and last-mile fulfilment, loyalty and customer data, and retail media and performance marketing.

Saudi Arabia is an unusually interesting market for this audience: card and digital payment penetration has risen sharply through the mada network and instant-payment rails, e-commerce has grown quickly from a low base, and the regulatory environment under the Saudi Central Bank has actively licensed payment institutions and open-banking providers. Attendees are merchants and retailers, bank and fintech product teams, payment service providers, e-commerce operators and the technology vendors serving them.
whatToExpect: A two-day exhibition and conference with multiple content stages, a startup and innovation zone, and demonstration areas for payment and retail technology. Expect merchant and retailer buyer traffic, pre-arranged meetings and evening networking.
venueAddress: Riyadh Front, Airport Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Athar Festival 2026
tagline: The Saudi Festival of Creativity, gathering the Kingdom's advertising, marketing and creative industries.
shortDescription: Athar - Saudi Festival of Creativity runs 24-25 November 2026 at Crowne Plaza RDC in Riyadh, with over 150 speakers and 80 brand activations across four content streams.
description:
Athar - Saudi Festival of Creativity is the Kingdom's main gathering for the advertising, marketing and creative industries, presented by Motivate Media Group and TRACCS. The fourth edition runs on 24 and 25 November 2026 at the Crowne Plaza RDC in Riyadh, with more than 150 speakers and around 80 brand activations.

The 2026 programme is organised into four streams. Creative Impact covers brand storytelling, advertising and marketing craft. Future Forward addresses artificial intelligence, machine learning and data-driven marketing. Screen and Influence explores media distribution, influencer marketing and content creation from an advertising perspective. Decoding Saudi offers an insider view of Saudi market dynamics, cultural shifts and creative ambitions for brands entering or scaling in the Kingdom.

The festival also runs the Athar Awards, which in 2026 expanded to include a Sports Campaign category with a jury of more than 80 industry veterans, and the Maheerah programme, now in its fourth year, which develops Saudi women in the creative industries. Athar matters because Saudi Arabia has become one of the largest advertising markets in the region, with rapid growth in local production, influencer commerce and sports and entertainment sponsorship.
whatToExpect: A two-day festival format with multiple stages, brand activation spaces and awards programming rather than a trade exhibition. Expect agency and brand-side attendance, creative work showcases, workshops and heavy networking.
venueName: Crowne Plaza Riyadh RDC Hotel & Convention
venueAddress: Riyadh Digital City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: AERO Middle East and Sand and Fun 2026
tagline: The Middle East's largest general aviation airshow, at Thumamah Airport north of Riyadh.
shortDescription: AERO Middle East x Sand & Fun runs 24-28 November 2026 at Thumamah Airport in Riyadh, combining a general aviation trade show with live flying displays and public experiences.
description:
AERO Middle East x Sand & Fun is a general aviation airshow and trade exhibition held from 24 to 28 November 2026 at Thumamah Airport north of Riyadh. It is organised by the Saudi Aviation Club in partnership with Messe Frankfurt Saudi Arabia, combining the international AERO general-aviation brand with the club's established Sand & Fun flying event.

The show covers light and business aircraft, helicopters and rotorcraft, avionics and instrumentation, flight training and pilot services, maintenance and MRO, drones and advanced air mobility, and airfield and FBO infrastructure. It is billed as the largest general aviation event in the Middle East, mixing a business and investment exhibition with live flying displays, aerobatics and interactive public experiences.

General aviation is a deliberate growth area for Saudi Arabia. The Kingdom is expanding private and business aviation infrastructure, has liberalised aspects of recreational flying and skydiving, faces a large national pilot and technician training requirement to staff its airline expansion, and is developing regional airstrips to support tourism destinations. Thumamah Airport, home of the Saudi Aviation Club, is the natural venue for that ecosystem to gather.
whatToExpect: An airfield-based event with static aircraft displays, exhibitor chalets and hangars, and daily flying and aerobatic displays. Expect a mix of trade visitors on business days and public spectators, plus flight-training and career pathway activities.
venueAddress: Thumamah, north of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Saudi Aviation Club with Messe Frankfurt Saudi Arabia

title: Noor Riyadh 2026
tagline: The world's largest light art festival, illuminating sites across the Saudi capital.
shortDescription: Noor Riyadh returns for its sixth edition in late 2026, installing large-scale light artworks by international and Saudi artists across multiple sites in the capital.
description:
Noor Riyadh is the annual light art festival produced by Riyadh Art under the Royal Commission for Riyadh City, and is described as the world's largest light art festival. The sixth edition returns in late 2026, following the pattern of previous years in which the festival has run for two to three weeks from late November into December.

Each edition commissions dozens of light artworks by Saudi and international artists installed across multiple sites in the capital. Recent editions have used the Al-Hukm Palace district, King Abdulaziz Historical Center, metro stations at King Abdullah Financial District, Al Faisaliah Tower and the JAX District in Diriyah, with a companion exhibition of light-based art. The festival holds numerous Guinness World Records, including for the largest LED structure and the longest distance covered by a laser light show.

Noor Riyadh sits inside Riyadh Art, a programme to install a very large number of permanent public artworks across the city, so the festival doubles as an annual public showcase and a talent pipeline for that permanent collection. It is free to attend, draws millions of visits, and has become a significant driver of night-time economic activity across restaurants, transport and retail during its run.
whatToExpect: Free open-air light installations across multiple districts, visited on self-guided trails with shuttle and metro links, plus a curated indoor exhibition and public programme of talks and tours. Expect very large evening crowds and family attendance.
venueAddress: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Riyadh Art, Royal Commission for Riyadh City

title: Global Logistics Forum 2026
tagline: The Ministry of Transport's international forum on supply chains, trade and logistics corridors.
shortDescription: The second Global Logistics Forum runs 29 November to 1 December 2026 in Riyadh, organised by the Ministry of Transport and Logistic Services with a parallel supply chain forum.
description:
The Global Logistics Forum (GLF) is organised by the Saudi Ministry of Transport and Logistic Services, with the second edition running in Riyadh from 29 November to 1 December 2026. It is convened alongside a supply chain forum, giving the Kingdom a combined platform on transport, logistics and international trade.

The forum brings together transport ministers, port and airport authorities, shipping and airline executives, rail operators, freight forwarders and 3PLs, manufacturers and retailers with large supply chains, and multilateral trade bodies. Programming covers trade corridors and connectivity, multimodal integration, supply chain resilience and near-shoring, customs and trade facilitation, logistics technology and automation, and sustainable transport.

Saudi Arabia's stake is its National Transport and Logistics Strategy, which aims to make the Kingdom a global logistics hub linking Asia, Europe and Africa. That programme includes major port expansion, the land bridge rail project connecting the Red Sea and Gulf coasts, special economic and logistics zones, and the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor in which Saudi Arabia is a central participant. GLF is the venue where those national plans are presented to the international logistics industry and where corridor partnerships are negotiated.
whatToExpect: A ministerial-level forum with plenary sessions, sectoral panels and bilateral government meetings, supported by an exhibition of logistics operators, ports and technology providers. Expect international transport ministry delegations and corridor partnership announcements.
venueAddress: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Ministry of Transport and Logistic Services

title: Saudi Intermobility Expo 2026
tagline: The Kingdom's largest road and smart mobility exhibition, formerly Gulf Traffic.
shortDescription: Saudi Intermobility Expo runs 30 November to 2 December 2026 at Riyadh Front, gathering over 7,000 mobility professionals and more than 100 exhibitors.
description:
The Saudi Intermobility Expo, formerly Gulf Traffic, is the Kingdom's leading road and smart mobility exhibition, organised by Informa Connect and held from 30 November to 2 December 2026 at Riyadh Front. It brings together more than 7,000 mobility professionals and over 100 exhibitors.

The scope covers road infrastructure and construction, traffic management and intelligent transport systems, road safety and enforcement technology, parking systems, street lighting and smart city infrastructure, public transport and bus systems, micromobility, and the data platforms that underpin urban mobility planning.

The Saudi market context is substantial. Riyadh has opened one of the world's largest new metro systems and is expanding bus networks, road-safety improvement is a national priority given historically high traffic fatality rates, and municipalities across the Kingdom are procuring intelligent transport and enforcement systems. Visitors include municipal and transport authority engineers, road contractors and consultants, traffic safety specialists, and technology suppliers serving city and highway operators across the Gulf.
whatToExpect: An exhibition of road infrastructure, traffic technology and mobility systems with live equipment displays, plus a conference programme on road safety and smart mobility. Expect municipality and transport authority delegations and contractor attendance.
venueAddress: Riyadh Front, Airport Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Health Tourism Future Forum 2026
tagline: Riyadh's forum on medical and wellness tourism, at the Fairmont Riyadh.
shortDescription: The Health Tourism Future Forum takes place 30 November to 2 December 2026 at Fairmont Riyadh, addressing medical travel, wellness tourism and healthcare destination development.
description:
The Health Tourism Future Forum is a Riyadh-based conference on medical and wellness tourism, scheduled for 30 November to 2 December 2026 at the Fairmont Riyadh. It brings together hospital groups, medical travel facilitators, insurers, tourism authorities, wellness operators and investors.

The agenda covers the practical machinery of medical travel: accreditation and quality assurance, patient pathway and case management, cross-border insurance and payment, visa and travel facilitation, wellness and preventive health resorts, and the marketing and referral networks that route patients internationally. It also addresses the reverse flow, meaning Saudi patients treated abroad and the domestic capability needed to retain that spending.

Saudi Arabia has explicit ambitions here. The Health Sector Transformation Program aims to raise domestic clinical capability and quality, private hospital groups have expanded rapidly, the Kingdom has been building destination wellness assets in AlUla, the Red Sea and Diriyah, and tourism policy targets high-value visitor segments. Combining a large domestic patient base with new luxury hospitality creates a credible medical and wellness tourism proposition that this forum exists to develop.
whatToExpect: A hotel-based conference with panels, case studies and B2B meetings between hospitals, facilitators and insurers, plus a compact exhibition. Expect hospital executives, wellness resort operators and tourism authority participation.
venueAddress: Fairmont Riyadh, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Black Hat MEA 2026
tagline: The region's largest cybersecurity event, running under the banner 'Infosec on the Edge'.
shortDescription: Black Hat MEA 2026 takes place 1-3 December 2026 at the Riyadh Exhibition & Convention Centre in Malham, combining technical briefings, trainings and a large security vendor exhibition.
description:
Black Hat MEA is the Middle East and Africa edition of the Black Hat brand, the long-established information security conference series, and has become the largest cybersecurity event in the region. The 2026 edition runs from 1 to 3 December at the Riyadh Exhibition & Convention Centre in Malham under the banner 'Infosec on the Edge', organised by Tahaluf with the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones.

The event follows the Black Hat structure of paid technical trainings preceding the main conference, a briefings programme of vetted original security research, and a large business hall of security vendors. Content spans offensive security and red teaming, cloud and identity security, OT and industrial control system protection, threat intelligence, application security, AI security and adversarial machine learning, and national-level cyber defence.

Its scale reflects both regional threat exposure and Saudi investment. Gulf critical infrastructure in energy, finance and government has been a persistent target of sophisticated attacks, and Saudi Arabia has built out national capability through the National Cybersecurity Authority alongside a fast-growing domestic security industry. Black Hat MEA also runs a hacking competition and community village programme that has become a significant talent-identification channel for the regional security workforce.
whatToExpect: Paid hands-on training courses ahead of the main days, technical briefings from vetted researchers, and a large business hall of security vendors and national pavilions. Expect capture-the-flag competitions, community villages, and a mix of practitioner and CISO audiences.
venueAddress: Malham, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Tahaluf with Black Hat and SAFCSP

title: Saudi Rehab Expo 2026
tagline: Rehabilitation, assistive technology and disability care exhibition in Riyadh.
shortDescription: The Saudi Rehab Expo runs 1-3 December 2026 in Riyadh, covering rehabilitation equipment, assistive technology, mobility aids and disability care services.
description:
The Saudi Rehab Expo is a specialist exhibition for rehabilitation, assistive technology and disability care, organised by 1st Arabia Tradeshows and Conferences and held from 1 to 3 December 2026 in Riyadh. It covers physiotherapy and rehabilitation equipment, prosthetics and orthotics, mobility aids and wheelchairs, assistive and accessibility technology, home care products, and rehabilitation centre design and services.

The event addresses a market shaped by specific Saudi policy. The Authority of People with Disability was established to coordinate services and enforce accessibility standards, universal-design requirements have been introduced into building codes and public facilities, and rehabilitation capacity is being expanded through both government health clusters and private providers. Road traffic injury rates have also historically created substantial rehabilitation demand.

Visitors include rehabilitation and physiotherapy clinicians, hospital and clinic procurement teams, care home and special education operators, insurers, charitable and non-profit organisations serving people with disabilities, and families purchasing directly. Exhibitors are equipment manufacturers and distributors, assistive technology companies, and service providers, with a growing digital-health component covering tele-rehabilitation and remote monitoring.
whatToExpect: An exhibition of rehabilitation and assistive equipment with hands-on trial areas, alongside clinical and service provider stands. Expect clinician and caregiver attendance, accessibility technology demonstrations and awareness programming.
venueAddress: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Saudi Coffee and Chocolate Exhibition 2026
tagline: Riyadh's consumer and trade festival for speciality coffee, chocolate and confectionery.
shortDescription: The Saudi Coffee & Chocolate Exhibition runs 1-5 December 2026 at Princess Nora Bint Abdulrahman University in Riyadh, with over 300 exhibitors from more than 40 countries.
description:
The Saudi Coffee & Chocolate Exhibition is a combined trade and consumer event held from 1 to 5 December 2026 at Princess Nora Bint Abdulrahman University in Riyadh, attracting more than 300 local and international exhibitors from over 40 countries.

The show pairs two categories with very high Saudi consumer engagement. Coffee spans traditional Arabic preparations, the fast-growing speciality café segment, domestic cultivation in the Jazan highlands where Khawlani coffee holds UNESCO intangible heritage recognition, and roasting and brewing equipment. Chocolate and confectionery covers premium and artisanal makers, dates and dessert products, ingredients, and gifting formats that are commercially significant around Saudi social and religious occasions.

Programming typically includes barista and latte-art competitions, cupping and tasting sessions, chocolate-making demonstrations, and business sessions on sourcing, franchising and café operations. Attendees include café and roastery owners, importers and distributors, hospitality buyers, home-business entrepreneurs — a category that has grown significantly through social commerce in Saudi Arabia — and large numbers of consumer visitors over the five-day run.
whatToExpect: A five-day exhibition with continuous tasting, competition stages, roasting and chocolate demonstrations and direct retail sales. Expect a mixed trade and consumer audience, family attendance in the evenings and long queues at popular producers.
venueAddress: Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: MDLBEAST Soundstorm 2026
tagline: The Middle East's largest music festival, staged in the desert at Banban outside Riyadh.
shortDescription: MDLBEAST Soundstorm returns to Banban outside Riyadh in early December 2026, the region's largest electronic and contemporary music festival with multiple stages.
description:
MDLBEAST Soundstorm is the largest music festival in the Middle East, produced by MDLBEAST and staged at a purpose-built desert site at Banban on the northern edge of Riyadh. The 2026 edition returns in early December, with tickets released well ahead of the line-up announcement.

The festival is built around multiple large stages programming electronic dance music alongside hip-hop, pop and Arabic artists, with production values comparable to the biggest international festivals. Past editions have drawn attendances in the hundreds of thousands across the run and have featured headline acts from the top tier of global touring artists, alongside a deliberate emphasis on Saudi and regional DJs and producers.

Soundstorm's significance goes beyond the weekend. MDLBEAST operates year-round as a music company with a record label, artist management, a booking agency and the XP Music Futures industry conference, and it has been central to building a professional music industry in Saudi Arabia from a standing start. The festival is also one of the largest logistical operations in the Saudi events calendar, employing thousands of temporary staff and driving significant hotel, transport and hospitality demand in Riyadh.
whatToExpect: A large-scale desert festival site with multiple stages, art installations, food and beverage villages and camping-adjacent infrastructure. Expect shuttle transport from Riyadh, late-night programming, and international and regional headline acts across the weekend.
venueAddress: Banban, north of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

title: Red Sea International Film Festival 2026
tagline: The Kingdom's flagship film festival, staged in the historic Al-Balad district of Jeddah.
shortDescription: The sixth Red Sea International Film Festival runs 3-12 December 2026 in Al-Balad, Jeddah, combining competition screenings with an industry market and professional programme.
description:
The Red Sea International Film Festival is Saudi Arabia's flagship film event, staged by the Red Sea Film Foundation in the UNESCO-listed Al-Balad district of Jeddah. The sixth edition runs from 3 to 12 December 2026, with early registration opened well in advance for industry participants.

The festival programmes competitive and out-of-competition sections spanning Arab, African and Asian cinema alongside international premieres, with juries drawn from global filmmaking. Around the screenings sits a substantial professional layer: the Red Sea Souk market for project financing and sales, the Red Sea Fund which invests directly in Arab and African productions, the Red Sea Lodge development programme for emerging filmmakers, and a talent and industry programme of masterclasses and panels.

The festival has become one of the most consequential events in Arab cinema because of the capital behind it. The Red Sea Fund is a meaningful source of production and post-production finance for filmmakers across the Arab world and Africa, and the festival's market has produced real deals rather than only publicity. Staging it inside the restored Al-Balad heritage district also links it directly to Jeddah's cultural regeneration, with screenings and events using historic buildings and squares.
whatToExpect: Ten days of screenings across cinema venues and heritage locations in Al-Balad, with red-carpet premieres, filmmaker Q&As and an industry market. Expect a professional accreditation track alongside public ticketing, plus masterclasses and evening events.
venueAddress: Al-Balad, Historic Jeddah, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia

title: Formula 1 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix 2026
tagline: Formula 1 at the Jeddah Corniche Circuit, with a rescheduled slot under discussion after the April cancellation.
shortDescription: The Formula 1 stc Saudi Arabian Grand Prix was originally set for 17-19 April 2026 at the Jeddah Corniche Circuit but was cancelled amid regional conflict; F1 has been reported as evaluating a December slot.
description:
The Formula 1 stc Saudi Arabian Grand Prix is held at the Jeddah Corniche Circuit, a 6.1 km street layout along the Red Sea waterfront that is among the fastest street circuits in Formula 1 and is raced at night under floodlights. The Kingdom has hosted the race since 2021 under a long-term agreement, with the event promoted by the Saudi Motorsport Company.

The 2026 running was originally scheduled for 17 to 19 April but was cancelled along with the Bahrain Grand Prix amid regional conflict, on safety and logistics grounds. Unlike Bahrain, the Saudi round has been widely reported as a candidate for rescheduling later in the season, with a December slot at Jeddah discussed alongside a corresponding shift to the Abu Dhabi finale. As of mid-August 2026 no revised date had been formally confirmed by Formula 1 or the FIA, so the December window listed here is provisional.

When it runs, the Grand Prix is one of the largest single events in the Saudi sporting calendar, combining the race weekend with a concert programme featuring international headline artists, fan activations and hospitality. It anchors a wider Saudi motorsport strategy that also includes Formula E, the Dakar Rally, Extreme E and a purpose-built permanent circuit planned at Qiddiya.
whatToExpect: A night race weekend on a fast street circuit with grandstand and hospitality tiers along the Corniche, plus a major concert programme after track sessions. Confirm the revised date before booking, as the rescheduled slot had not been formally announced at the time of writing.
venueAddress: Jeddah Corniche, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia

title: Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games 2026
tagline: Riyadh 2026, the sixth Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games with around 3,000 athletes.
shortDescription: The sixth Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games run 13-21 December 2026 in Riyadh, with 45 National Olympic Committees and around 3,000 athletes across 18 sports and 25 disciplines.
description:
The Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games, branded Riyadh 2026, is the sixth edition of the continental multi-sport games organised under the Olympic Council of Asia. Competition begins on 11 December with the opening ceremony on 13 December and the closing ceremony on 21 December 2026.

The Games bring together 45 National Olympic Committees and around 3,000 athletes competing in 18 sports across 25 disciplines with 122 medal events. The programme is built around indoor and martial arts disciplines including jujitsu, karate, kickboxing, muaythai, taekwondo and wrestling, alongside indoor sports such as futsal, handball, 3x3 basketball, and esports, which has become a standard fixture of Asian multi-sport programmes. The athletes' village is located at Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University.

For Saudi Arabia the Games are a significant staging post. The Kingdom is scheduled to host the 2029 Asian Winter Games at Trojena in NEOM, the 2034 Asian Games in Riyadh, the AFC Asian Cup in 2027 and the FIFA World Cup in 2034. Delivering a multi-sport event with 45 delegations tests venue readiness, athlete services, anti-doping, transport and international broadcast operations well ahead of those commitments.
whatToExpect: Nine days of competition across indoor venues in Riyadh with opening and closing ceremonies, an athletes' village and international broadcast. Expect ticketed sessions, national supporter groups and a large volunteer and operations workforce.
venueAddress: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: Olympic Council of Asia with the Saudi Olympic and Paralympic Committee

title: Saudi Smart Home and Furnishings Expo 2026
tagline: Smart home technology and furnishings exhibition at Dhahran Expo in the Eastern Province.
shortDescription: The Saudi Smart Home & Furnishings Expo runs 14-17 December 2026 at Dhahran Expo in Dammam, covering home automation, appliances, furniture and interior products.
description:
The Saudi Smart Home & Furnishings Expo is held from 14 to 17 December 2026 at Dhahran Expo in Dammam, serving the Eastern Province consumer and trade market. It covers home automation and smart devices, security and access systems, energy management, appliances, furniture and furnishings, lighting, and interior finishing products.

The Eastern Province is a distinctive market: it combines the industrial economy around Dhahran, Dammam, Khobar and Jubail with a large, relatively affluent household base including Saudi Aramco employees and a substantial expatriate professional population. That supports demand for premium home technology and furnishings at a level comparable to Riyadh and Jeddah.

The smart home category has grown quickly across Saudi Arabia on the back of high smartphone penetration, new-build housing delivered under the Sakani programme with provision for automation, and utility interest in demand management as electricity tariffs have been reformed. Visitors include homeowners and consumers, interior designers and fit-out contractors, developers specifying smart systems into new residential stock, and retailers and distributors seeking product lines.
whatToExpect: An exhibition combining trade stands and consumer retail, with working smart-home demonstration rooms, appliance displays and furniture room sets. Expect a mixed trade and public audience with evening family attendance across the four days.
venueAddress: Dhahran Expo, Dammam, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia

title: Jeddah E-Prix Season Opener 2026
tagline: Formula E opens its 2026-27 season with a double-header on the Jeddah Corniche Circuit.
shortDescription: Formula E's 2026-27 season is provisionally scheduled to open with a double-header at the Jeddah Corniche Circuit on 18 and 19 December 2026, rounds one and two of the championship.
description:
The ABB FIA Formula E World Championship returns to the Jeddah Corniche Circuit on 18 and 19 December 2026 for a double-header that is provisionally scheduled to open the 2026-27 season as rounds one and two. The dates come from Formula E and the FIA's first provisional calendar for the season, so they remain subject to change.

Staging the season opener in Saudi Arabia is a notable step up from the Kingdom's previous mid-season slot. Formula E has raced in Saudi Arabia since 2018, first at Diriyah where it introduced the first night races in the championship's history, and more recently on the Jeddah street circuit shared with Formula 1. The races are run under floodlights along the Red Sea waterfront.

The championship's presence supports Saudi Arabia's electric-mobility narrative, which includes PIF's stake in Lucid Motors and its Jeddah plant, the Ceer national EV brand, and the national charging infrastructure rollout. For the teams and manufacturers involved, the Saudi rounds function as a commercial and government-engagement platform for the wider Gulf market as well as a race weekend.
whatToExpect: A street-circuit double-header with practice, qualifying duels and two evening races, plus fan zones, driver appearances and concert programming. Expect an accessible open-paddock format and grandstand seating along the Corniche.
venueAddress: Jeddah Corniche, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia
organizerName: ABB FIA Formula E World Championship

title: King Abdulaziz Camel Festival 2026
tagline: The world's largest camel racing and beauty competition, in the Al-Dahna desert north-east of Riyadh.
shortDescription: The King Abdulaziz Camel Festival returns in December 2026 at Al-Sayahid in the Al-Dahna desert, combining camel racing, beauty judging, heritage markets and cultural programming.
description:
The King Abdulaziz Camel Festival is the largest camel event in the world, staged at Al-Sayahid village in the Al-Dahna desert between Rumah and Al-Rumahiyah, roughly 120 kilometres north-east of Riyadh. It returns in December 2026, typically running for between 30 and 45 days from early December into January.

The festival's two competitive pillars are camel racing and the Mazayen beauty competition, in which camels are judged on physical characteristics including head shape, neck length, hump and colour, with prize money running into hundreds of millions of riyals across categories. Judging is now supported by veterinary screening and technology to detect prohibited cosmetic interventions.

Around the competition sits a purpose-built festival city covering more than 225 square kilometres, with multiple race tracks, a large accommodation zone, a heritage market, a museum, poetry and dialogue venues, a falconry area and traditional food. The festival is run by the Camel Club under a mandate to preserve camel heritage while developing it into an organised sport and an economic sector covering breeding, veterinary services, dairy and tourism.
whatToExpect: Desert race tracks with grandstand viewing, beauty competition arenas, a heritage souk and museum, and traditional food and poetry venues. Expect early-morning racing, large domestic crowds at weekends, and a purpose-built temporary city in the dunes.
venueAddress: Al-Sayahid, between Rumah and Al-Rumahiyah, Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia

title: Winter at Tantora 2026
tagline: AlUla's flagship winter cultural festival across Old Town, Maraya and the desert.
shortDescription: Winter at Tantora returns to AlUla in December 2026, staging concerts at Maraya and Thanaya, heritage dining at AlUla Fort and cultural programming across the oasis.
description:
Winter at Tantora is AlUla's flagship winter festival and one of the most established cultural events in Saudi Arabia, run by the Royal Commission for AlUla as part of the AlUla Moments calendar. The festival returns in December 2026, following a pattern of running from mid-December into January.

Programming is spread across AlUla's most distinctive settings. Major concerts are staged at Maraya, the mirror-clad concert hall that holds a Guinness World Record as the largest mirrored building, and at the open-air Thanaya amphitheatre. The Shorfat Tantora series brings live music to the rooftops of the AlJadidah Arts District, Old Town Nights combines heritage storytelling with fine dining at the historic AlUla Fort, and the AlManshiyah Carnival provides family programming with traditional games and parades.

The festival takes its name from the Tantora sundial in AlUla Old Town, historically used to mark the agricultural seasons, and its programming deliberately links contemporary entertainment to that agricultural and heritage calendar. Winter at Tantora has been central to establishing AlUla as a destination, filling hospitality capacity in peak season and drawing international visitors to a region better known for the Nabataean tombs at Hegra.
whatToExpect: Ticketed concerts at Maraya and Thanaya, heritage dining experiences at AlUla Fort, rooftop music in the arts district and family carnival programming. Expect bookable experiences with limited capacity, desert and oasis settings, and cool evening weather.

title: Retail Show Saudi 2026
tagline: Riyadh trade show for retail technology, store operations and omnichannel commerce.
shortDescription: Retail Show Saudi is held 7-8 October 2026 in Riyadh, covering retail technology, point of sale, store design, supply chain and omnichannel commerce for the Saudi market.
description:
Retail Show Saudi is a Riyadh trade event for the retail industry, scheduled for 7 and 8 October 2026. It covers retail technology and point-of-sale systems, store design and fixtures, inventory and supply chain software, payments and checkout, loyalty and customer engagement, and omnichannel and e-commerce operations.

The Saudi retail market is the largest in the GCC by population and is undergoing rapid structural change. Modern trade continues to take share from traditional retail, e-commerce penetration has grown quickly, quick-commerce and delivery platforms have become mainstream in the major cities, and international brands have entered at pace through franchise and joint-venture structures. Retailers face simultaneous pressure to digitise operations and to meet Saudisation requirements in store-level employment.

Visitors are retail operators and store development teams, e-commerce and digital managers, supply chain and merchandising specialists, franchise groups, and shopping centre operators. Exhibitors include retail software vendors, hardware and fixture suppliers, logistics and fulfilment providers, and payment and loyalty platforms. The event complements the larger Seamless Saudi Arabia show by focusing more tightly on store operations and retail technology.
whatToExpect: A compact two-day exhibition and conference focused on retail technology and operations, with vendor stands and demonstration areas. Expect retail operator and franchise group attendance, practical case-study sessions and supplier meetings.

title: Saudi Film Confex 2026
tagline: The Film Commission's conference and exhibition for the Saudi screen industry.
shortDescription: Saudi Film Confex is the Film Commission's annual industry conference and exhibition in Riyadh, expected to return in the autumn of 2026 following its October pattern.
description:
Saudi Film Confex is the annual conference and exhibition of the Saudi Film Commission, part of the Ministry of Culture, held in Riyadh. It combines an industry conference with a trade exhibition of production equipment, services and screen-sector organisations, and is expected to return in the autumn of 2026 in line with its established October timing.

The event is aimed squarely at building industrial capacity in the Saudi screen sector. Programming covers production and post-production services, studio and location infrastructure, cash rebate and incentive schemes for international productions, distribution and exhibition, financing and co-production, and skills development for crew and technical roles. It functions as the meeting point between the Film Commission's policy instruments and the working industry.

The context is a screen sector rebuilt from almost nothing since cinemas reopened in 2018. Saudi Arabia now has a substantial exhibition circuit, a production incentive scheme aimed at attracting international shoots, studio developments including facilities in NEOM and AlUla, and a growing pipeline of Saudi features and series commissioned by regional and global streamers. Attendees include producers and production service companies, equipment suppliers and rental houses, broadcasters and streamers, cinema operators, and film students and emerging crew.
whatToExpect: A conference programme of industry panels and workshops alongside an exhibition of production equipment, service companies and screen-sector bodies. Expect rebate and incentive briefings, co-production meetings, and recruitment and training activity for crew roles.
